newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina condemns TV show's Dirty War scoop.
newsitem.headline: Argentina condemns TV show's Dirty War scoop.

text.p: The Argentine government and human rights groups on Tuesday condemned a television channel's sensational re-enactment of the interrogation and torture of a journalist abducted and killed in the "Dirty War."

America TV scored a scoop on Monday night by obtaining a military transcript of an interrogration from the 1976-83 dictatorship when thousands of people "disappeared" -- presumably abducted, tortured and killed by death squads.

But the new show "Fenomeno," hosted by journalist Mauro Viale and soccer star Diego Maradona, included a dramatisation of the June 1977 abduction of journalist Rafael Perrotta and his torture with electric shocks.
Two children of the late editor of El Cronista Comercial newspaper were present in the studio for the live show.

"I saw part of the programme last night and it was really horrible," President Carlos Menem told reporters. Human Rights Undersecretary Alicia Pierini called it "scandalous ... that the 'desaparecidos' (disappeared) should be used as merchandise."
Human rights campaigners who long demanded to know the whereabouts of the military's victims accused the program's makers of using their painful past to boost ratings.
Adolfo Perez Esquivel, who won the Nobel Peace Prize for his campaign against the brutality, said it was "dangerous to use such a serious thing to increase your audience."

The junta leaders, who were jailed after the return of democracy in 1983 but freed under an amnesty declared by Menem in 1989, insist all documents on the repression were burned. But reports have recently emerged of secret military files on the abductions being smuggled out to Switzerland via Spain.
The TV show's producer, Fabian Doman, said he was also shown "a list of 200 people, of whom 20 are 'desaparecidos' and the rest were just investigated by military intelligence."
Activists demanded the producers be summoned by courts "to say where they got it, if there is more information and if these are the famous files and who is responsible."
A copy of the transcript obtained by Reuters appears to be a verbatim account of Perrotta's interrogation after his abduction in Buenos Aires' tony Recoleta district in 1977.
Stamped "Strictly Secret and Confidential," it starts:

"With much pain and shame, I, Rafael Andres Perrotta, will make a spontanous declaration about my relation with people of the PRT (Revolutionary Workers' Party)." It goes on to detail the journalist's alleged links with the guerrilla group.
Reuters also got a copy of a security service telegram faking Perrotta's kidnap and relaying a $1 million ransom demand. His family paid $85,000, but never saw him again.
